messages:
maria_oncall: Heads-up: rolling AZ-level cache rebalance + control-plane routing cleanup scheduled WED 23:00-01:30 UTC. Window is split into 3x 30m passes per-AZ with 15m cooldowns. Expect brief p95/p99 latency increases and occasional 502s for <2m during vswitch transitions.

alex_sre: Thanks. Which AZs are first? Any change to model routing rules?

maria_oncall: Order: az-a -> az-b -> az-c. No permanent routing logic changes. We'll temporarily lower per-route connection reuse timeout to force healthy reconnects and verify session eviction works. Model routing will failover to cross-AZ warm nodes if local p99 > 600ms for >90s.

kevin_infra: Operational note: We'll kick off a small traffic shuffle to reassign hot shards after each AZ pass. This will create a spike in KV store reads; watch redis-read-latency and serving-cpu.

fiona_sre: Can we pre-warm KV prefixes so spikes are bounded? Or will that defeat the validation?

maria_oncall: We'll pre-warm a subset (10%) of prefixes as a sanity measure, but the goal is to exercise rebalance so most prefixes will experience cold misses.

liam_net: Network ops: there will be a BGP flap simulation for 2m during the start of AZ-b pass to validate routing fallback. We'll annotate metrics with tag network_experiment=true.

carla_pm: Support & comms: should we post a status page message? Any SLA impact we need to disclose publicly?

maria_oncall: Public status: short notice — "Planned infrastructure maintenance may cause intermittent elevated latencies for some routes between 23:00-01:30 UTC. Enterprise customers on Dedicated pools unaffected." No SLA credit expected; not a partial outage. Support blurb coming in 1h.

kevin_infra: SLO tweak (internal): for non-paid tier, p99 latency target temporarily relaxed to 600ms for the maintenance window per-AZ. Alerts suppressed for synthetic=true tags. Paid tiers unchanged.

alex_sre: Abort criteria proposal: 1) sustained error-rate >0.7% for 5m, 2) p99 > 3x baseline for >15m with no improvement after revert, 3) control-plane API error 5xx >1% for >2m. If triggered we abort and roll back config toggles.

maria_oncall: Add: if redis-cluster rebalancers exceed 70% CPU for >3m, pause. Runbook updated with commands.

fiona_sre: Runbook snippet: ```
# quick abort commands
kubectl -n controlplane rollout undo deploy/edge-router --to-revision=previous
# disable rebalance flag
kubectl -n infra set env configmap/edge-config REBALANCE_ENABLED=false
# scale back synthetic generator
kubectl -n loadgen scale deployment/synth-gen --replicas=1
```

srebot: scheduled: maintenance-#6012 created by maria_oncall for 2024-09-04T23:00Z->2024-09-05T01:30Z

kevin_infra: We'll emit metrics: maintenance.phase={az-a,az-b,az-c}, maintenance.synthetic=true for the synthetic bursts. Dashboards will have a shaded window.

liam_net: I'll be on the network bridge from 22:30 UTC to watch the BGP experiment.

alex_sre: I'll run post-pass verification checklist: - endpoint p50/p95/p99 baseline diff - kv hit-rate - replica sync lag - control-plane 5xx. Will post short summary after each AZ.

carla_pm: Approved. I'll push support blurb and schedule a short status page update.

maria_oncall: TL;DR actions: 1) Bridge from 22:30, 2) Support/status blurb, 3) Dashboards mark synthetic, 4) Abort criteria in runbook, 5) Post-pass summaries per-AZ. Post-maintenance incident summary expected within 48h.

alex_sre: No objections. Will mute non-critical alerts and add synthetic tag to our monitoring rules.

kevin_infra: I'll run the pre-warm job 30m before each pass and confirm KV hit-rate baseline.

maria_oncall: Thanks all. Ping me in thread if anything changes. Reminder: keep all rollback commands ready and labelled in the runbook.
